entities.summary:
The Younger Lady is the informal name given to an ancient Egyptian mummy discovered within tomb KV35 in the Valley of the Kings by archaeologist Victor Loret in 1898. This mummy, designated as KV35YL and 61072, has been identified as the mother of pharaoh Tutankhamun and a daughter of pharaoh Amenhotep III and his Great Royal Wife Tiye. The mummy's DNA tests have revealed a complex ancestry, sparking significant interest in Egyptology and ancient Egyptian royal families. 

The discovery of The Younger Lady has significantly advanced our understanding of ancient Egyptian royal succession and the intricate relationships within the royal family. The mummy's presence in the Valley of the Kings, a necropolis that has yielded numerous important archaeological finds, underscores the importance of this site in the study of ancient Egyptian history. 

The Younger Lady's discovery has also shed light on the life and reign of pharaoh Tutankhamun, one of the most famous pharaohs of ancient Egypt. The mummy's DNA tests have revealed a close genetic relationship with Tutankhamun, confirming the mummy's role as his mother. 

In conclusion, the discovery of The Younger Lady has been a groundbreaking moment in the field of Egyptology, providing new insights into ancient Egyptian royal history and the lives of its most prominent figures.
